# Writing a `design-system` page

Generated from `design-system`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Lives at** `design/design-system.md` — a singleton, one per design wiki
- **Authorship** `curated` — an agent may draft it; a human approves
- **Freshness** stale after 180d
- **Template version** 2 — set `template-version: 2`

## Frontmatter

Required on this type beyond the base fields (`title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`):

- `realizes`

The template also scaffolds `template-version`, `icon-catalog`, `sources`, `related`, `invalidates`, `origination`, `confidence` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

`owner:` is fixed to `design` — do not change it.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}}. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

The body also carries 5 placeholders written in angle brackets — `<how the voice flexes in this situation; what the copy does and avoids>`, `<the call>`, `<the traits that hold in every context, each with what it means for the words>`, `<validation error / system error / warning / …>`, `<what is unresolved>`. Each stands for content you write; replace every one, including in a row whose other cells you have already filled. Leaving one is an error (`unsubstituted-placeholder`).

## Where this type may link

This page lives in `design/` (layer 2).

You may link to `domain/`, `product/` — and to other pages in `design/`.

You may not link to `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

## Sections

Keep every heading, in this order: `## Overview`, `## Principles`, `## Voice and tone`, `## Foundations / tokens`, `## Component index`, `## Interaction patterns`, `## Governance & contribution`, `## Decisions`, `## Open questions`, `## Related`.

**These may not be answered `None.`** — they must carry content: `## Voice and tone`.

**Table columns you may not drop:**

- `## Voice and tone` — `Situation` | `Tone`
- `## Decisions` — `Decision` | `State` | `Decided`
- `## Open questions` — `Question` | `Owner` | `Resume condition`

## What the audit checks on this page

Because of the declarations above: template-sections, section-order, required-section-content, table-columns. Every page is also checked for empty sections, heading restatement, callout types and code pointers. Run `/wiki-conformance-audit` to see the full list with its verdict.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
